title: Parasite’s Ram-Don
description: A pivotal scene in the 2020 Oscar-nominated film involves cooking this dish, also known as jjapaguri. The Hollywood Reporter enlisted some expert help for a recipe to make at home. In Bong Joon Ho's genre-bending thriller Parasite, Kim Chung-sook (Chang Hyae-jin) is tasked with making ram-don with steak for the soon-to-arrive Park family. “When you make it and try it once, you will crave it quite often because it's so fast and easy to make. But it can be still quite healthy if you add some protein to it.”
ingredients: 1 or 2 heads of broccoli, in smallish pieces
1 cup or so of chopped up or shredded “protein” – pork, chicken, beef, etc
1 teaspoon red chili paste or gochujang
2 helpings of udon or rice noodles
1 or 2 helpings of onion or garlic chips
1 or 2 dashes of sesame seeds (maybe toasted)
Some fresh herbs, such as cilantro or mint
directions: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a skillet.
Add most of the chopped scallions and garlic, and red chili paste; cook over moderately high heat until scallions are softened.
Add any vegetables you like (such as thinly sliced zucchini, onion, carrot, broccoli, red pepper, or mushroom). Stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes, until softened and nicely cooked.
Cook udon noodles in a pot of boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain; add noodles to skillet.
Add any cooked protein you like soy sauce, black bean paste, brown sugar, plum sauce, and fish sauce. Toss together.
Stir-fry over high heat until everything is heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.

Plate the food, and add freshly ground pepper, fried garlic chips (optional) and additional chopped scallions; sprinkle with sesame seeds and toasted sesame oil. Garnish with any fresh herbs you like.
